canonical.name: Mac Lane's original coherence package had more than this page's two axioms, and this page explains exactly which later items retire the extras
The pentagon and the triangle are independent axioms
The tensor-unit endomorphisms become commutative by an Eckmann-Hilton argument
Modules over a monoid object and their morphisms form a category
Monoid objects in abelian groups are rings
Modules over a commutative ring form a monoidal category
A poset with finite meets is a strict monoidal category
The reverse construction and the opposite-category construction are different and both are needed later
The bare phrase monoidal functor is source-ambiguous, so the page fixes the lax/strong/strict trichotomy explicitly
Only parenthesized tensor words are defined before coherence, and the unbracketed notation must wait for MA-13
The Isbell skeleton argument blocks any attempt to strictify by simply identifying isomorphic objects
The pointed-set smash-product example is omitted from this scaffold because the library still has no published pointed-set home that would let the theorem close honestly on disk
canonical.reason: The design marked the pointed-set theorem contingent on a published home for pointed sets, and this workspace still has none. Keeping the item now would force the page to depend on vocabulary and examples the library has not actually built.
